memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron who died when they approached the LORD. The LORD said to Moses: "Tell your brother Aaron that he is not to come whenever he chooses into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, or else he will die. For I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover." - Lev 16:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before a single instruction is given, God reminds Aaron of the worst day of his life.

Nadab and Abihu were his sons. They had offered unauthorised fire before the LORD, and they died (Lev 10:1-2). Aaron had buried two children. Now God says, in effect: remember what happened, and understand why these instructions matter.

That may sound harsh. It is actually mercy. God is not taunting a grieving father — He is protecting him. He does not want to bury a third son. So He speaks plainly: not whenever you choose, or you will die.

We live in a time that finds this difficult. We prefer a God who is entirely approachable and never dangerous. But a God who could be approached carelessly would not be worth approaching at all. His holiness is not a barrier to His love; it is what makes His love astonishing.

And notice why the danger exists: I will appear in the cloud. The peril is not that God is absent. It is that He is present.

The wonder of the gospel is not that God became safe. It is that Christ made the way in, and now we may approach the throne of grace with confidence (Heb 4:16). Not casually. Confidently — which is a very different thing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you lost any sense of God's holiness in how you approach Him?
2. What is the difference between coming casually and coming confidently?
3. How does God's warning here show His care rather than His coldness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy, and I have often come to You carelessly. Thank You that Christ has opened the way. Teach me to approach You with both confidence and reverence. Amen.
